cohort: Pregnant women who delivered at the study center over a year period, comparing primigravidae (first-time mothers) to multigravidae (mothers with previous pregnancies)
finding: Primigravidity was associated with a statistically significant increase in several obstetric complications, including hypertensive disorders, prolonged pregnancy, prolonged labor, oxytocin augmentation, cephalopelvic disproportion, obstructed labor, instrumental delivery, cesarean delivery, and neonatal unit admission.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were significantly higher in primigravidae compared to multigravidae (P = 0.011).
